A silver bullet against cancer

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... an amazing medical breakthrough in our backyard

Unique Selling Point:
New revolutionary South African developed treatment for cancer

Summary:
A new cancer drug that promises less side effects has been developed in South Africa.

The UJ3 drug, which forms part of the promising silver-based cancer drugs, has been successfully tested in both rats and in human cells in the lab.

In a new research, published in peer-reviewed scientific journal Biometals - UJ3 is shown to be as effective against human esophageal cancer cells, as the standard chemotherapy drug, Cisplatin, which is mainly used to treat a widely-used chemotherapy drug in use today.

Further information:
A new cancer drug that promises less side effects has been developed in South Africa.

The UJ3 drug, which forms part of the promising silver-based cancer drugs, has been successfully tested in both rats and in human cells in the lab.

In a new research, published in peer-reviewed scientific journal Biometals - UJ3 is shown to be as effective against human esophageal cancer cells, as the standard chemotherapy drug, Cisplatin, which is mainly used to treat a widely-used chemotherapy drug in use today.

Esophageal cancer cells are known to become resistant to current forms of chemotherapy. The new drug is so potent that it requires a 10 times lower dose to kill cancer cells. It also focuses more narrowly on cancer cells rather than healthy cells.


“The UJ3 complex is as effective as the industry-standard drug Cisplatin in killing cancer cells in laboratory tests done on human breast cancer and melanoma, a very dangerous form of skin cancer, as well,” says Professor Marianne Cronjé, Head of the Department of Biochemistry at the University of Johannesburg.

“In rat studies, we see that up to 3 grams of UJ3 can be tolerated per 1 kilogram of bodyweight. This makes UJ3 and other silver phosphine complexes we have tested about as toxic as Vitamin C,” says Professor Reinout Meijboom, head of the Department of Chemistry at the University of Johannesburg (UJ).

Researchers have described the new discovery as a breakthrough for cancer treatment in SA.

If UJ3 becomes a chemotherapy drug in future, the lower dose required, lower toxicity and greater focus on cancer cells will mean fewer side effects from cancer treatment.

They said UJ3 appears to target the mitochondria, resulting in programmed cell death to kill cancer cells – a process called apoptosis. When a cancer cell dies by apoptosis, the result is a neat and tidy process where the dead cell’s remains are “recycled”, not contaminating healthy cells around them, and not inducing inflammation.

Certain existing chemotherapy drugs are designed to induce apoptosis, rather than “septic” cell death which is called necrosis, for this reason.

Cancer cells grow much bigger and faster, and make copies of themselves much faster, than healthy cells do. In this way they create cancerous tumors. To do this, they need far more energy than healthy cells do.

UJ3 complex and the others in the family are based on silver. This makes the starter materials for synthesizing the complex far more economical than a number of industry-standard chemotherapy drugs based on platinum.

Research on UJ3 and other silver thiocyanate phosphine complexes at the University is ongoing.

Press Release:


The Silver Bullet
A revolutionary drug discovery by scientists at the University of Johannesburg is taking the fight against cancer to new levels. Experts are calling it the silver bullet, a remarkable compound which could stop cancer cells in their tracks. Carte Blanche analyses this astonishing medical development.


Script:


V/O:
Here at the University of Johannesburg a chance discussion over a glass of red wine between a chemist and a cancer researcher has led to an astounding medical breakthrough that could change the course of cancer treatment worldwide.

The researcher is Professor Marianne Cronje. She is involved in anti-cancer research.

And the chemist is Prof Reinout Meijboom. At the time he was exploring the crystal structure of a family of silver compounds.

His wife was a colleague of Marianne, and one day they were having dinner with red wine, and purely by accident talked about his chemical compounds.
Meijboom:
And during a conversation with Marianne over a glass of red wine – a good Shiraz if I remember correctly – she suggested “Give those compounds to me and we’ll do some anti-cancer testing”.
V/O:
This has led to a discovery here in South Africa that has the medical world abuzz and has attracted international attention.
Marianne:
It was completely serendipitous, you know, I think in the process we basically stepped on the needle in the haystack.
V/O:
And the needle in the haystack they accidentally stepped on is a completely new way to kill cancer cells that is set to revolutionize cancer treatment.
LINK
And what makes it even more remarkable is that the two of them are from completely different and unrelated disciplines.
V/O:
Meijboom is the Head of the Department of Chemistry and Cronje is one of South Africa’s foremost cancer researchers. Her interest has been in killing cancers cells in an alternative way to that of chemotherapy or radiation. Traditional cancer therapies are problematic in many ways. It is prohibitively expensive, costing hundreds of thousands of rands. And in addition, it also has severe side effects.
Marianne:
The problem with most chemotherapeutic drugs, and that’s why we see so many side effects, is that these cancer drugs are not specific. So you end up targeting normal cells as well.
LINK:
It is really difficult to kill cancer cells because they function unlike normal cells in the body.
V/O:
These are normal cells. Each has a nucleus where the DNA is located, and in the cells are mitochondria, providing energy to the cell. Normal cells are programmed to grow to a certain size and also have a built-in mechanism or programme to self-destruct when necessary.
Marianne:
This form of cell death is known as apoptosis, and an apoptosis is a form of programmed cell death. It is very controlled. In your body there are approximately 6 billion cells every day that gets turned over that has to be recycled and the content that is removed from the cells, the breaking down of the process, this is basically recycled.
LINK:
So, apoptosis plays a vital role in maintaining the health of the body by eliminating old cells, unnecessary cells, and unhealthy cells.
V/O:
But cancer cells defy apoptosis signals. They do not undergo natural or programmed cell death. Instead, they grow bigger and out of control, using huge amounts of energy. Eventually they form tumours.

Traditional cancer treatments mostly target the DNA of cancer cells in order to kill them. But it is not a precise treatment.
Marianne:
Well, it is a little bit like a shotgun approach, it is a blunderbuss approach. You are shooting everything. What you are hoping to do is you hope to target the tumour or the cancerous cells but unfortunately it is so that you end up targeting normal cells as well.
V/O:
In addition, this kind of cell death causes a significant and undesirable inflammatory response in a patient’s body.

In her career, Marianne focused on ways to induce apoptosis, or natural cell death in cancer cells. It would eliminate the inflammatory response. 9 years ago, she was doing researching on indigenous plants such as the Kankerbossie or Cancer Bush, the Sutherlandia frutescens.
Marianne:
And we wanted to see if compounds, or extract of the Sutherlandia could induce apoptosis in cancer cells. And we tested them on oesophageal and breast cancer cells and they work and they induced apoptosis, yes.
V/O:
It was at that time she had the fortuitous red wine discussion with Prof Meijboom and asked him for samples of the silver compounds to test. Meijboom was sceptical, because most known chemo therapy treatments are based on platinum.
Meijboom:
My initial reaction was it was not going to work because there are two papers in the literature showing that some other members of this group were not as active as the prevailing platinum based drug.
V/O:
However, Marianne was insistent and kept on asking for examples of the compounds.
Marianne:
One day he came and he brought me 5 compounds and said: “There you go. Now you can test them”
LINK
Marianne gave the 5 substances to a senior student to test on lab grown human cancer cell. Number one and two did nothing. But when number three was tested, the student called Marianne.
Marianne:
And she came to me and said “Prof, you’d better come and look at this. These cells are changing shape and we know that when cancer cells change shape and they become rounded, they look like little balls under the microscope we know that this is indicative of the apoptotic process. I had a look and I said I don’t believe this, please try this again. And she did and she did it two, three, four, five times and she said “No, Prof, these compounds look really interesting”.
V/O:
Each time it was clear – the compound, called UJ3 was inducing natural cell death in cancer cells. Incredibly, out of a possible 3 thousand compounds in the silver phosphine family, the third one they tested was the silver bullet.

Marianne introduced us to Dr Zelinda Engelbrecht who showed us the compound in action.
Zelinda:
So this is actually the oesophageal cells, the cancer cells. You can see a lot of cells clumped close to each other. And the other one… This is the same cells that were treated with UJ3. So you will see there are lots of spaces in between because when the cells die, they detach. So you only seeing the cells her that are still attached but they are in the process of dying.
V/O:
Amazingly UJ3 targets only cancer cells and does not target healthy cells at all.

The dosage required to kill cancer also surprised them.
LINK:
UJ3 is highly effective in very small doses.
V/O:
But while it is deadly to cancer, it is non-toxic to humans. And what is more, it is amazingly cheap and easy to create, so it could possibly in future revolutionize the cost of cancer treatment. Over the last 9 years they have tested UJ3 on a variety of cancers in vitro and also in rats. It killed the cancer every time.

However, this UJ3 silver compound is not to be confused with colloidal silver which is available in pharmacies.
Marianne:
Colloidal silver is a completely different compound from the compounds that we have started testing in the lab. Colloidal silver … if you use a large amount of colloidal silver you will actually end up looking like a Smurf. You’ll turn blue.
LINK:
The next step will now be to go to clinical trials to see if UJ3 will be as effective in living human beings as it was in the lab and in rats.
V/O:
However, setting up clinical trials to test it on humans is very complex and subject to all kinds of ethical protocols to identify participants. Both Meijboom and Cronje warn, that while this is a massive breakthrough, it will still take many years before UJ3 could be available as a cancer treatment.
